# Nx
Nx is a powerful open-source build system that provides tools and techniques for enhancing developer productivity, optimizing CI performance, and maintaining code quality.
Documentation is here: https://nx.dev/getting-started/intro 

![20240523125742](data:image/png;base64,)
## Using Nx with Angular
Angular mono repo tutorial is available here: https://nx.dev/getting-started/tutorials/angular-monorepo-tutorial
Nx itself consists of technology-agnostic package with core functionality, plugins which provide code generation and executors for specific technology and VS Code extension. But it is important to install [compatible nx version](https://nx.dev/nx-api/angular/documents/angular-nx-version-matrix) to use angular plugins.
To install the package globally run the following command:
``` sh
npm install nx@latest -g
```
Global package will redirect all the commands to the local package installed in the current project.
For angular code generation `@nx/angular` plugin can be used. It is also possible to setup all the required staff using package `create-nx-workspace`. For angular we should run the following command:
``` sh
npx create-nx-workspace@latest angular-monorepo --preset=angular-monorepo
```
It will create `angular-monorepo` folder with mono repo in it.
Basically nx commands have the following format:
![Pasted image 20240523133343](data:image/png;base64,)
So, to serve the application we should run the following command:
``` sh
nx serve application-name
```
It is also possible to run dev server on a specific host with disabling host check:
``` sh
nx serve application-name --host location.sub.domain.net --disable-host-check
```
### Code generation
Nx plugins usually provide generators. Nx `@nx/angular` plugin provides generators for Angular apps. To see the list of generators run the following command:
``` sh
nx list @nx/angular
```
Examples of using `@nx/angular` code generators are described below:
``` sh
# Use --dry-run switch to preview the changes

# Creating new application in the monorepo
nx g @nx/angular:app application-name --directory=apps/application-name

# Creating new library in the monorepo
nx g @nx/angular:library library-name --directory=libs/library-name --standalone
```
### Troubleshooting
Errors with inconsistent packages could be listed using `nx report` command. In the end of the report nx may suggest to run automatic migration.
